name: SARES-DEIM: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Meets DETR for Clutter-Aware SAR Ship Detection

raw_payload.title: SARES-DEIM: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Meets DETR for Clutter-Aware SAR Ship Detection
raw_payload.summary: Ship detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery is challenged by coherent speckle noise, complex coastal clutter, and the prevalence of small-scale targets. Conventional detectors, primarily designed for optical imagery, often exhibit limited adaptability to SAR-specific degradation and suffer from the loss of fine-grained ship signatures during spatial downsampling. To address these limitations, we propose SARES-DEIM, a domain-aware detection framework grounded in the DEtection TRansformer (DETR) paradigm. Central to our approach is SARESMoE (SAR-aware Expert Selection Mixture-of-Experts), a module leveraging a sparse gating mechanism to selectively route features toward specialized wavelet, spatial, and frequency-oriented experts. This sparsely activated architecture enhances clutter-aware representation while keeping the active inference cost controlled. Furthermore, we introduce the Space-to-Depth Enhancement Pyramid (SDEP) neck to preserve high-resolution spatial cues from shallow stages and improve the localization of small targets. Experiments on HRSID and SAR-Ship-Dataset show that SARES-DEIM achieves competitive results across both public benchmarks, with more prominent advantages on the challenging HRSID dataset. Specifically, SARES-DEIM achieves 76.4% mAP50:95 and 93.8% mAP50 on HRSID, while keeping the active computation at 72.6 GFLOPs and 136.5 FPS on a single NVIDIA A40 GPU with batch size 8; the batch-size-1 latency is 37.6 ms.
